about: Points to handle, shown in the admin (Inbox › To do › Points, admin.js renderPoints; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md "Points to handle"). Written by agents: questions for an IMR trainer, nomenclature points, discrepancies between sources, content questions for Pierre. Pierre's state per point (status, notes, the trainer's answers) is his curation, in curation.json points, never here. The list's order is the priority: the most important first. Wording: neutral questions, never that IMR is wrong (rule C1). Fields: id (stable, never reused), kind (a key of kinds), subj (coral or fish), at (date added, Manila), title (the list's line), q (the question in plain words, shown big), ctx (context lines, folded), ask (the answer field under each photo), photos ([{f: a photo id of data.json or cand.json, with src, a, o, t as fallback when it leaves the app} or {none: why a slot is empty}]), src (sources: [{t, u?}]).

points.title: Which corals does IMR label Astrea in ReefCloud?
points.q: Which ReefCloud label would you give each of these corals?
ctx: Which corals does IMR label "Astrea" in ReefCloud: only Astrea curta and A. annuligera (Astrea in WoRMS and iNaturalist), or also the former Phymastrea, now Favites colemani, F. valenciennesii and F. magnistellata in WoRMS and iNaturalist, and maybe Paramontastraea salebrosa?
Slide 62's "refer to Astrea / Phymastrea" suggests the second; only a trainer can say.

Photos: 1 Astrea curta from abroad (one of the app's Astrea photos); 2 Favites colemani from the Philippines (one of the app's 4 F. colemani photos, under Favites); 3 Plesiastrea peroni from Dauin (a look-alike, from the Coral Finder's extra genera); 4 Pierre's Favites colemani near Dauin (iNaturalist observation 406194912); 5 and 6 Astrea curta from abroad (two of the app's Astrea photos, from two other observations), which Pierre doubts are Astrea; 7 Favites valenciennesi near Dauin (one of the app's Favites photos, a candidate Pierre added), which Pierre asks whether it is Astrea.
Until the answer the app changes nothing: its 4 F. colemani photos stay under Favites.
Waiting on this answer (Q47): if IMR calls these corals Astrea, Pierre's F. colemani near Dauin can serve as an Astrea photo (rule S2: his species-level photos stay usable as photos).

points.title: Slide 62: "refer to Astrea / Phymastrea"
points.q: Slide 62 says "refer to Astrea / Phymastrea". Corals of the World's Phymastrea species (colemani, valenciennesi, magnistellata) are Favites species in WoRMS, and Astrea's are under Astrea. Which corals does the slide mean?
ctx: Favites and its neighbours, for Pierre to raise with IMR (research report of 2026-11-04; only species present in the Philippines by Pierre's rule, rule C6; the app keeps the lecture's wording and adds "Other sources" notes, tools/apply_favites.py).
Slide 62: "refer to Astrea / Phymastrea". Corals of the World's Phymastrea pages (colemani, valenciennesi, magnistellata) are Favites species in WoRMS; Astrea's are under Astrea.
See also: Which corals does IMR label Astrea in ReefCloud?

points.q: Slide 61's notes say Favites buds exclusively extra-tentacularly; Huang et al. 2014 give Favites both intra- and extra-tentacular budding, and Dipsastraea intra only. How should RAs use budding to tell them apart?

points.title: Paliform lobes: Goniastrea or Favites
points.q: The lecture uses paliform lobes to tell Goniastrea from Favites. Corals of the World shows a well-developed crown in some Favites and in Paragoniastrea russelli and Paramontastraea salebrosa, all recorded in the Philippines. How should RAs use paliform lobes?
ctx: Paliform lobes as the Goniastrea / Favites separator (slide 40 notes, Goniastrea's ID tip): a well-developed crown also appears in F. pentagona and F. colemani, often in F. vasta (Corals of the World), and in Paragoniastrea russelli and Paramontastraea salebrosa, all recorded in the Philippines.
Part of the Favites block (research report of 2026-11-04).
